items.title: Paul Beaulieu Interview, 1960-06-11
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] ...somebody published one called Porter and Stiegel.

ctx.x: The one who composed, who is the author, composer of high society.

There was another arrangement I had, I think, published by Melrose in Chicago. But several people published it in late years. Yeah. And somebody published one called Porter and Stiegel. But just to think.

That piece had to come down here. And Robichaud had to try. And such people as, like I tell you, George Marquis, and Bad Frank, and finally P. Guhoud and others. Yes. And made that variation. Kindle that is known all over the United States. All over the world now. The world. It's a New Orleans tune. Yeah. It's a New Orleans tune from the fact that New Orleans made it famous. But it wasn't composed in New Orleans. It's going to show you how it came here. Yeah. I was told. I was told that tobacco was found here…
